key_insight: Single-crystal Ti-15Mo shows weak but inverted elastic anisotropy and strongly orientation-dependent yield onset that simple Schmid/CRSS rules do not predict.
engineering_relevance: For β-titanium component design and texture engineering, crystal orientation can shift indentation modulus and yield behavior enough to matter even when hardness changes only slightly.
method: EBSD to index surface normals and select orientations near ⟨111⟩, ⟨124⟩, ⟨011⟩, ⟨023⟩, and ⟨013⟩
Nanoindentation to measure hardness, indentation modulus, yield onset, and strain-rate sensitivity
Strain-rate-jump testing to estimate activation volume and infer deformation mechanisms
evidence_signal: Across the sampled orientations, modulus varied by about 10%, yield onset by 41%, and hardness by only 6.6%, with activation volumes of 18–31 b³.
watch_item: The proposed retained athermal ω-phase explanation is plausible but indirect, so confirming the mechanism would require dedicated phase/structural evidence beyond indentation data.
paper_title: Orientation-Resolved Nanoindentation of Single Crystal Ti-15Mo: Inverted Elastic Anisotropy and Yield-Onset Behavior Beyond Simple CRSS Predictions
